Whether approved for reporting?1 For the applicant: Mr. Nishant Khidtta, Advocate For the respondent: Mr. Tejasvi Sharma, Addl. A.G with Mr. Mohinder Zharaick, Addl. A.G and Ms. Leena Guleria, Dy. A.G assisted by Inspector/SHO Jyoti,
First Women Police Station, Shimla.
Virender Singh, Judge.

By way of present application, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.PC'), applicant-Ankush has sought his release, on bail, during the pendency of trial, in case FIR No. 18 of 2023, dated 5th September, 2023, registered with Women Police Station BCS, Shimla, H.P., under Sections 363, 376 and 354- A of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 8 of the 1 Whether the reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'POCSO Act').

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. According to the applicant, he is an innocent person and has falsely been implicated in the present case.
The applicant has pleaded that he is a young man of 20 years and keeping him, in the judicial custody, will adversely affect his future.
3. Apart from this, number of undertakings have also been given on behalf of the applicant, for which, the applicant is ready to abide by, in case, released on bail, during the pendency of the trial.
4. The applicant has earlier tried his luck before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Shimla, H.P., as well as, before this Court.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Shimla, H.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, his application was dismissed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge vide order dated 27.09.2023, whereas, the bail application filed before this Court has been dismissed as withdrawn on 05.10.2023.

5. According to the applicant, the investigation in the present case is complete and the police has filed the report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
6.
On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to release him on bail during the pendency of the trial.

7. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that on 05.09.2023,
the complainant along-with child victim and her husband appeared before the police and moved a complaint, disclosing therein, that she is residing with her family and her husband, is Tour and Travel Agent by profession.
They have been blessed with two children (one son and one daughter).
The child victim is elder one aged about 16 years, whereas, the son is about 13 years.
The child victim is studying in Government Senior Secondary School in +1 class. 7.1.

On 02.09.2023, the child victim informed the complainant that she was called by her friends, who requested the child victim to come to the school on Sunday, as, they have to do the rehearsal and practice for Teacher's Day function.
Consequently, the complainant send her to school.
On that day, about 7.30 p.m., when the complainant came back, the child victim was found to be frightened.

When the complainant inquired from her as to why she came back during late hours, then, she has not disclosed anything,
but, she was found to be frightened.

7.2. In the evening of Monday, when the complainant again inquired from the child victim, then, she has disclosed that on Sunday when, she was at place 'X' (name withheld) one Sahil Thakur (applicant) met her who enticed away her and took her to the old bus-stand, where, he took her in a room in the hotel.
In the room, the applicant has started doing obscene acts with her by putting his finger in her vagina.

7.3. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to take action against the accused, upon which, FIR under Sections 363 and 376 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act was registered and thereafter, criminal machinery swung into motion.
The child victim was medico legally examined by the doctor and the doctor opined that recent sexual assault cannot be ruled-out, in this case.
7.4. The statement of child victim and her parents under Section 161 Cr.P.C were recorded.
On 05.09.2023, the applicant was arrested at about 8.20 p.m.
He was also medico legally examined.
The spot map was prepared.
7.5. On 08.09.2023, the child victim was produced before the Court for recording her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
The documents pertaining to date of birth of the child victim were obtained and her date of birth was found to be 01.11.2007.

7.6. During investigation, the police also found the commission of offence punishable under Section 354-A IPC and Section 8 of the POCSO Act, as such, provisions of both the sections were added in this case.
7.7. On 12.09.2023, the owner of the hotel where the applicant allegedly took the child victim had produced the recording of CCTV.
Perusal of the same shows that on 03.09.2023, the accused along-with the child victim had gone to the said hotel at about 5.00 p.m. and got booked a room.
At about 6.38 p.m. accused and child victim had left the said hotel.

2 7.8.

During investigation, it was found that the child victim was studying in +1 class and on the occasion of Teacher's Day, the child victim and her friends had made a plan on 02.09.2023, to come to the school for dance practice.
She has requested her friends to get permission from her parents.

Consequently, on 02.09.2023, during evening, the friend of the child victim had requested the mother of the child victim to permit her to come to school on 03.09.2023 for dance practice,
whereas, they were not called to school for practice.

7.9. Due to the holiday, school was closed, however, the child victim and her friends had done the dance practice in the ground of Primary School and at about 2.00 p.m., the child victim took the phone of her friend on the pretext of making an urgent call to her parents and after making call, she has returned the phone to her friend.
The child victim, as well as, her friends had done dance practice till 4.00 p.m.
Thereafter, her friends had gone to their home.
When the child victim and her friends were on way, back to their home applicant met the child victim and the child victim disclosed the name of applicant to her friends as Anku from Solan.

When, the child victim and her friends had gone to their home and the applicant again met the child victim, he took her to the old bus-stand, where they had gone to the hotel and stayed in Room No. 102 where, the applicant had allegedly done the crime.
7.10. It is further case of the police that the investigation, in the present case, is complete and the report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C has been filed on 20.10.2023.

7.11. Lastly, it has been apprehended that in case, the applicant is released on bail, he may coerce the witnesses, as well as,
the child victim.
Hence, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.
8. The investigation, in the present case, is complete as after the completion of investigation, the police has submitted the report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
This fact is sufficient to conclude that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required by the police.

Moreover, keeping in view the age of the applicant, which has been mentioned in the status report as 20 years, keeping him in the judicial custody, that too, for indefinite period, in the company of hardened criminals, would certainly affect his career.
9. The role allegedly played by the applicant in the commission of the offence will be proved during the course of trial.
The chances of commencement and conclusion of trial against the applicant, in near future are not so bright.
As such, no purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in the judicial custody.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as narrated by the police, in the status report, this Court is of the view that the applicant is able to make out a case for bail in his favour.
11. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

12. Consequently, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No. 18 of 2023, dated 5th September, 2023, registered with Women Police Station BCS, Shimla, H.P., under Sections 363,
376 and 354-A of IPC and Sections 4 and 8 of POCSO Act, on his furnishing personal bail bond, in Ankush vs State Of H.P on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140524748/
3 the sum of 30,000/-, with one surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court/CJM Sirmaur at Nahan/Judicial Magistrate, Shillai/Duty Magistrate.

entities.text: Women Police Station BCS, Shimla, H.P.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 13. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations, are confined, only, to the disposal of the present bail application.
14. It is made clear that the respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions, is found to be violated by the applicant.

15. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Jail,
District Jail, Kaithu through e-mail, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e-prison software.

16. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of Jail, District Jail, Kaithu is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary, DLSA,
Shimla.

entities.text: Superintendent of Jail, District Jail, Kaithu
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: The Superintendent of Jail, District Jail, Kaithu is further directed that if the applicant fails to furnish the bail bonds, as per the order passed by this Court, within a period of one month from today, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.
November 10, 2023 ( Virender Singh )
